description:
## What

Define `pkix_aia::AiaFetcher` trait per PKIX-zkjb constraints 1, 3, 5.

```rust
pub trait AiaFetcher {
    fn fetch(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError>;

    fn batch_fetch(&self, uris: &[&str]) -> Vec<Result<Vec<u8>, AiaError>> {
        uris.iter().map(|uri| self.fetch(uri)).collect()
    }
}
```

Key shape decisions (locked):

- `&self` not `&mut self` — admits caching wrappers via interior mutability or Arc
- Sync (no async on the core trait — async lives in adapter crates)
- Returns `Vec<u8>` of certificate DER bytes (not parsed Certificate — parsing is the caller's job; the trait is "fetch bytes")
- `batch_fetch` default-impl loops to `fetch` — implementers pipeline when it helps
- No timeout parameter on the trait (timeout is a fetcher-impl concern, configured at construction time)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pkix_aia::AiaFetcher` trait public, with `fetch` required method and `batch_fetch` default-impl
- [ ] Trait `Sync + Send` (auto if impls are; document the expectation)
- [ ] Rustdoc explains: caller responsibility for parsing returned bytes; trait is dumb-bytes-fetch
- [ ] Doctest showing how to wrap a fetcher with a caching layer (caller side, demonstrates &self enables this)
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry on pkix-aia

## Out of scope

- HTTP impl (PKIX-zkjb.5)
- verify_chain integration (PKIX-zkjb.6)
- NoAiaFetcher (PKIX-zkjb.4)

## Cross-references

- PKIX-zkjb (parent, constraints 1, 3, 5)
- pkix-revocation::RevocationChecker (existing trait pattern reference)
- pkix-path::SignatureVerifier (existing trait pattern reference)
